progress.$description: Linear progress bar — a filled track. Built 2026-09-07 for the Explore Degrees wizard's two genuinely-missing cases: the determinate coverage bar in the results header ('your credits already cover 6 of 20 requirement areas') and the indeterminate bar under 'Checking your classes…'. **Deliberately NOT the wizard's step indicator** — Stepper already exists for exactly that ('horizontal step indicator for a short multi-step flow', inactive/active/complete with a filling connector), and a first pass that scoped a `segmented` variant here was corrected: numbered circles read clearer than anonymous segments, and two components for one job is how drift starts. Two modes on one recipe: determinate (a width the consumer sets, plus the ARIA value) and indeterminate (a travelling sliver, no value). Two heights only — sm for a bar that sits under other content, base where the bar itself is the message. Like Spinner, the indeterminate animation is NOT stopped by prefers-reduced-motion: it is the only signal that work is still happening. Deferred: a role axis (success/danger bars), segment labels, and a circular/radial form — nothing needs them.

radius.$description: Fully rounded at both ends, on the track and the indicator alike, so a nearly-empty bar still reads as a bar and not as a stray dot.

sm.$description: 4px — under a header or inside a card, where the bar is secondary to the numbers next to it.

base.$description: 8px — the default, for when the bar is the thing being looked at.

track.$description: The unfilled remainder. bg.neutral (gray.100) — the same quiet tint EmptyState's pill and the date chips use, so an empty bar reads as a placeholder rather than as a border.

indicator.$description: The filled part. Same brand blue every other 'this is happening / this is done' cue uses; deliberately not status.success, because a progress bar reports amount, not outcome.

sliverWidth.$description: How much of the track the travelling sliver covers. 40% reads as motion without ever looking like a real value.

label.$description: The optional caption above the bar (e.g. '6 of 20 requirement areas'). The bar itself never contains text.
